findings.title: Scope creep violates stated boundaries
findings.location: Section 0. Scope paragraph 1 and Project Shape tree
findings.evidence: "This spec defines how the add-in process talks to SolidWorks. Every SolidWorks COM call... flows through the abstractions defined here." followed by full tree including Tools/DocumentTools.cs, State/StateSerializer.cs, Events/EventRelay.cs, Lifecycle/, Undo/
findings.problem: The document claims narrow focus on STA queue + six service contracts yet specifies full add-in architecture, message dispatch, session management, undo, state capture and screenshot logic.
findings.why_it_matters: Creates brittle god-spec that will require coordinated changes across SPEC-03/04/05 whenever adapter details shift; contradicts "Depends on: SPEC-00 (module boundaries)".
findings.proposed_fix: Split adapter plumbing (queue, services, COM mapping) into its own document; move tool-specific, state, lifecycle, and bridge details to consuming specs.

findings.title: In-flight COM calls cannot be cancelled, breaking agent responsiveness assumption
findings.evidence: "COM calls cannot be interrupted. The worker runs the command to completion... The lifecycle layer (SPEC-03) treats this case by quarantining the eventual result."
findings.problem: Long-running operations (e.g. complex Extrude, GetFeatureTree on large assemblies) block the single STA queue with no preemption path.
findings.why_it_matters: An adversarial or malformed tool_call can freeze the entire CAD agent for minutes; contradicts "responsive" voice/agent loop implied by SPEC-05 dependency.
findings.proposed_fix: Document explicit per-operation timeout bounds and queue timeout escalation policy; remove claim that this is "the only correct model" without escape hatch.

findings.title: Screenshot sharing assumes perfect same-user filesystem context
findings.location: Section 7 Screenshot Directory Convention and 7.1 Path Format
findings.evidence: "the add-in (which runs in the same local user context as the orchestrator)" and path using %LOCALAPPDATA%\BSVoiceCAD\screenshots\{addinSessionId}
findings.problem: Breaks under UAC elevation, containerized orchestrator, remote desktop sessions, or antivirus locking LocalAppData; no fallback negotiation or in-memory transfer defined.
findings.why_it_matters: Core image ingestion path for SPEC-05 Anthropic API calls becomes silently unreliable; hash-mismatch path only logs warning and omits context.
findings.proposed_fix: Require explicit shared directory via config/env var with handshake; add memory-only transfer option for non-co-located processes.

findings.title: Hand-maintained deserializer creates permanent sync fragility
findings.location: Section 5.2 Solution and 5.3 Sync Test — ProtocolDeserializerSyncTests
findings.evidence: "The file is checked in to source control. It is NOT generated... kept in sync with the Protocol assembly via a build-breaking test."
findings.problem: Reflection-based test will fail on any Protocol change; rationale that "protocol changes are rare during the hackathon" does not survive post-hackathon evolution.
findings.why_it_matters: Introduces recurring source of build breaks and developer friction; alternative of shipping System.Text.Json 8.0+ via NetFx shim or separate polyfill was dismissed without analysis.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with source generator or single shared assembly containing both serializer and deserializer; remove reflection test.

findings.title: AddinSessionId generation depends on registry read that may be unavailable
findings.problem: HKLM read can fail under restricted user accounts, AppLocker, or non-Windows CI; no fallback or error behavior specified.
findings.why_it_matters: Breaks reconnect handshake and screenshot paths; collides with "Day-0 Validation" requirement that must pass before implementation starts.
findings.proposed_fix: Document fallback (e.g. random + persisted in SW property) and test under least-privilege account.

top_3_must_fix: Scope creep violating stated boundaries (Section 0 vs full project tree)
In-flight COM calls cannot be cancelled (Section 2.3)
Screenshot sharing assumes perfect same-user context (Section 7)
